label: Fact
headline: Sample: Fictional federal-style agency opens comment period on placeholder rule
dek: A sample US-politics article about an invented agency rule. It demonstrates how {{name}} explains comment periods and effective dates.
whatHappened: The Office of Placeholder Standards, a fictional agency invented for this sample, opened a 60-day comment period on a placeholder rule about public-record formats.
The sample notice says the rule would not take effect before a placeholder date next year.
whyItMatters: In this sample, a comment period is the stage where the public can respond before a rule is finalised, so the effective date is still open.
confirmed: The rule would not take effect before a placeholder date (sample notice).

attributed.claim: The rule will save agencies money.
attributed.attributedTo: the fictional Office of Placeholder Standards, in a sample summary

unknown: How many comments will be filed.
Whether the final rule will differ from the proposal.
